title: Imaging Built-in Electric Fields and Light Matter by Fourier-precession TEM
content: In recent years much progress has been made in the field of phase contrast imaging by exploiting real and diffraction space signals simultaneously. Most prominently, 4D-datasets obtained using fast pixelated detectors are analysed by centre of mass (COM) imaging or various ptychographic techniques [1, 2]. However, in these cases the sampling of the diffraction space is fixed and given by the detector geometry, ranging from 4-16 segments for differential phase contrast (DPC) detectors to larger pixel array detectors. In addition, especially in the case of DPC detectors with central holes, the dose in the centre of the Ronchigram does not contain much information and is often lost [3]. Thus, a technique would be desirable which allows for flexibility in the sampling of the diffraction space. This is offered by Fourier ptychography popular in the optics community, and which has been successfully applied to electron microscopy [4-6].
